t: No fiscal year 1979 funds may be withheld from a State under subpart 3 of part A of title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965 because of a failure of a State to meet the requirement of section 415C(b)(4) of that Act based upon the provisions of a State statute enacted prior to October 1, 1978.

fable.w: The section only bars withholding fiscal year 1979 grant funds from a State for failing to meet a statutory requirement because of a pre-existing State statute. The mention of a State is tempting, but the State appears only as a funding recipient, not as a party consulted before a federal decision. There is no comment period, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: No fiscal year 1979 funds may be withheld from a State under subpart 3 of part A of title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965

qwen_block.w: This section is a funding restriction that prevents the federal government from withholding funds from a State due to a specific compliance issue. It does not require the federal government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from any outside party (such as the State, the public, or experts) before making a decision. The interaction described is purely financial and regulatory, not participatory.
qwen_block.s: No fiscal year 1979 funds may be withheld from a State under subpart 3 of part A of title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965 because of a failure of a State to meet the requirement of section 415C(b)(4) of that Act based upon the provisions of a State statute enacted prior to October 1, 1978.

opus.w: This section only limits when the federal government can withhold grant funds from a State. It creates no process for States or other outside parties to consult with the government or weigh in on a federal decision. Mentioning a State as the grant recipient is not participation, because grants and benefits are excluded under the definition.
opus.s: No fiscal year 1979 funds may be withheld from a State under subpart 3 of part A of title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through:** The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section mentions a State and a federal decision about withholding funds. That reading fails. The provision only stops the federal government from withholding fiscal year 1979 grant funds because of an earlier State statute. It sets no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. The State is just the party that receives the grant money, not a participant in a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes a condition under which federal funds cannot be withheld from a state. It does not require the federal government to consult with the state, nor does it involve public comment, hearings, or advisory committees. The interaction described is a unilateral determination of fund eligibility based on statutory criteria, not a participatory process.
qwen_chat.s: No fiscal year 1979 funds may be withheld from a State under subpart 3 of part A of title IV of the Higher Education Act of 1965 because of a failure of a State to meet the requirement of section 415C(b)(4) of that Act based upon the provisions of a State statute enacted prior to October 1, 1978.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the section involves "States" and "funds," it implies some form of interaction or consultation regarding state compliance. However, the text is purely a waiver of a penalty (withholding funds) based on a specific timeline of state legislation. It does not require the federal government to consult with the state, nor does it grant the state a right to participate in a decision-making process. It is a substantive rule about fund eligibility, not a procedural requirement for participation.
